new_features.title: Give today's prompt a close time and count down to it
new_features.rationale: The screen runs a live countdown to the prompt's close, which means the fetch contract has to carry a close timestamp. E03-F1 defines one prompt per calendar day and never mentions a close time, and E03-F2 lists the card and its states without a timer.

/.note: E03-F2 and E03-F3 cover the prompt card and the already-submitted read, E02-F2 the session that gates the bounce, E01-F9 the bottom nav. The streak tile on this screen is E11-F2, which is ORANGE and blocked, so a GREEN daily screen currently depends on an ORANGE feature. Worth resolving before sprint 1.

/+not-found.note: E01-F9 asks for the full route graph reachable and error states that never leave a blank screen, and this restyled catch-all is exactly that. No journey aims here by design, so there is nothing to add.

new_features.title: Draw your own avatar and save it to the profile
new_features.rationale: This is the only DrawPad output that reaches the server, cropped to 256x256 and PATCHed as a base64 data URI on the user record. E04-F1 and E04-F2 build the canvas and the artwork capture but nothing covers the avatar use of them or the payload size that a user record now carries on every profile read. The screen also needs fixing before it is rebuilt: the drawable canvas is larger than the circle the avatar is cropped to, so a person can draw outside the circle and lose it. The capture on this page shows exactly that, with the figure's head and antennae outside the crop. The canvas should be the size of the avatar, not a square the crop is taken from.

/avatar.note: The canvas and the stroke capture are E04-F1 and E04-F2, reused unchanged with a circle mask and the full palette. The avatar itself has no feature. Worth flagging that squareAvatarDataUri is a no-op on native (src/lib/image.ts:15-22), so a native save PATCHes the full uncropped export.

new_features.title: Make submit safe to repeat
new_features.rationale: This is the only call in the app that unlocks a wall. The submission id is deterministic per user and prompt, which reads as an intended idempotency key, and neither E04-F4 nor E04-F5 says the write must upsert rather than fail on a duplicate key. The client's only protection is a submitting boolean disabling the button mid-flight.

/choose-channels.note: E05-F3 plus E04-F4 and E04-F5 cover the picker, the fan-out, and the unlock, and the screen correctly leaves membership and unlock enforcement server-side. The pinned-prompt confirmation branch here belongs to the new wall-pinned-prompt feature proposed on /draw, not to a second one.

/compose.note: E18-F4 is this screen. It says select tiles on a wall and compose a keepsake, and Eric's feedback inside it names the manual arrange-and-manipulate option that app/compose.tsx actually built. E12-F2 owns the selection interaction and says to build it once for both. This is not a gap, it is a GRAY blocked feature that the POC already shipped, which is the thing to raise in planning.

new_features.title: Create a wall and invite by email in one form
new_features.rationale: E05-F1 builds the channel model and the invitation-only join path on the backend. No feature builds the client form that names a wall, parses a comma-separated address list, and reports a per-address failure. That is the whole of app/create-wall.tsx and it is iOS work E05 does not currently carry.

/create-wall.note: E05-F1 and E02-F3 cover the server side of creating a wall and issuing invites. The client form has no feature at all, and it is the only door to wall creation in the app. Note the invite is theater in the POC, no email leaves the device (src/lib/simulatedInvites.ts), so the new feature must not be read as already built.

new_features.title: Draw against a wall-pinned prompt
new_features.rationale: The screen carries a second entry path that skips the daily prompt fetch and carries a wall id and prompt id straight through to a one-wall submit. E03-F2 describes only today's prompt and E05-F3 describes only the fan-out picker, so nothing in the backlog owns the pinned path even though it is built and shared with /choose-channels.

/draw.note: PR 63 read the narrow toolset here as a finding, on the assumption that a fuller set was waiting behind EXPO_PUBLIC_FULL_TOOLSET. It was not. E18-F1 was retired on 2026-09-01 and E04-F1 now states the client's decision outright, one brush and eight colors, so what this capture shows is the shipping tool set rather than a flagged-down version of something richer. The question is closed, not open.

new_features.title: Leave a text-only reflection on a past day
new_features.rationale: The wall lets a person answer a locked past day with text and no drawing, posting to POST /submit with no artwork (app/family.tsx:106-161, mounted at :360-362). E04-F3 sizes the 280-character story as a companion to a drawing, and E04-F5 enforces submit-to-unlock. Neither says what a drawing-free submission does to the unlock rule or to the streak.

/family.note: E05-F4 covers the grid and the day scroll, E05-F6 the heart, E11-F3 the archive branch, and E12-F2 the multi-select that feeds /compose. The text-only reflection is real, writes to POST /submit, and has no feature. The pack-prompt button at app/family.tsx:1092-1105 belongs to the prompt-pack gap recorded on the two pack screens.

/home.note: E05-F5 names this exact surface, the wall list plus the stats card, and E11-F2 and E11-F4 supply the numbers and the three locked badges the tile shows. The pending-invite row that opens /invite/[id] (app/home.tsx:204-206) is E02-F5. Nothing on this screen is outside those four.

new_features.title: Reach an invite from outside the app
new_features.rationale: E02-F5 says a person opens an invite link, and no such path exists. The only route into this screen is a tap on a badged wall row inside the signed-in app, so accepting an invite today needs an account you already have. The hosted landing page, the deep link, and the token are all unbuilt, which is the whole out-of-app half of the feature. The 2026-09-01 standup set the likely shape: a small static website, the way Scribl already links out to their own hosted pages, holding the pages the app cannot host, this invite screen among them. The flow is that adding somebody by email sends them an email, they follow a link to that static page, and once they log in to the app they see the invite waiting and accept it to join the wall. Three things need answers from Scribl before this can be built: what the email says and looks like, where its link lands, and whether the static site does anything beyond explaining the invite.

new_features.title: Decline an invite from the accept screen
new_features.rationale: The store's decline method does real work, including handing membership back through leaveWall, and no screen calls it. Not now only defers. Someone has to decide on purpose whether saying no outright ships.

/invite/[id].note: E02-F3 and E02-F5 cover the accept sequencing, which this screen already does correctly. What they do not account for is that the transport under the button is a single-device AsyncStorage illusion with no entry point from outside the app. PR 63's finding holds against the source.

new_features.title: Clear the canvas behind a confirmation
new_features.rationale: E04-F1 lists one brush, sizes, six inks and undo, then says nothing else. The screen also ships a trash control with its own confirm modal, and Eric's 2026-08-25 feedback leaves the trash button open, so the built behaviour has no feature to land in.

/onboarding/canvas.note: E04-F1 and E04-F2 own the Skia canvas and the raster capture, and E04-F1 now also owns the allowedColors seam that narrows the palette on this screen, since E18-F1 was retired. The capture's swatch count against E04-F1's settled eight colors is a build detail to reconcile on the screen, not an open product question any more. The clear control is new.

/onboarding/prompt-intro.note: E02-F4 names the prompt introduction and already logs the missing Get Inspired branch as Q10, which is the one thing the code comment here says is unbuilt. E03-F1 owns the fetch this screen reads.

/onboarding/ready.note: E02-F4 names the ready screen and E02-F5 owns landing on the invited wall. The onboarding-complete flag written here is the other half of the resume feature proposed at /splash, so it needs no feature of its own.

/onboarding/story.note: E02-F4 names the story input step and E04-F3 sets the 280-character cap this screen enforces. The sun glyph in the tile comes from seeded capture data on an unmerged branch, so it is a capture artifact, not missing backlog scope.

new_features.title: Resolve what the story fork screen looks like without record
new_features.rationale: E04-F3 says ship the write path and leave the record button out, but this screen is a two-card fork whose only reason to exist is that choice. Drop record and the screen has one button, so onboarding either loses a step or ships a card that goes nowhere.

/onboarding/story-select.note: E04-F3 and E18-F3 already hold the record decision and the parked voice pipeline, so the capability is housed. What is not housed is this screen, which E02-F4's eight-screen list never names and which stops making sense once record is cut. The record branch also pushes to /record with next=onboarding-walls, leaving the seven-step list entirely, so the straight-line flow diagram is only half right.

/onboarding/walls.note: E02-F4 names the wall explanation with its share-to checklist, E05-F1 and E05-F3 own the wall list and the multi-wall fan-out, E04-F4 owns the submit call fired here. This is where the first Scribl actually posts, not on the ready screen.

/onboarding/welcome.note: E02-F4 names the personalized welcome as screen 2 and E02-F5 owns getting the inviter's name into the copy. The screen does exactly those two things and nothing else.

new_features.title: Capture a voice note on a native build
new_features.rationale: Support detection checks getUserMedia and MediaRecorder, both web-only, so on device this screen can only ever show not available. E18-F3 calls voice notes greenfield and prices a full lane, and it does not say the web capture and upload already work while native has no capture path at all. /story-select also offers the microphone card on every platform with no signal before the tap.

/record.note: E18-F3 is the right home, and its framing is off in both directions. Real capture, real upload, and server-side byte and duration clamping already exist on web, while native has nothing. The doc comment in src/lib/storyLimits.ts:6-7 still calls voice capture stubbed, which understates what shipped.

new_features.title: Remove the AI enhancement controls from the response viewer
new_features.rationale: E18-F5 was retired on 2026-09-01, so the original and enhanced toggle and the regenerate action on this screen are controls for a capability the product no longer has. They sit behind AI_ENABLED and are off, which is why nobody has noticed them. Take them out rather than leaving dead UI behind a flag that reads as a pending feature.

/response/[id].note: E05-F4 names the detail view with the drawing, the story and the reaction affordances, and E05-F6 the single heart. The voice-note player belongs to E18-F3. The share button is F6's entry and lands in E12-F4. The one change here is a subtraction: the AI original and enhanced toggle belonged to E18-F5, which is retired, so those controls should come out.

new_features.title: Account and profile settings screen
new_features.rationale: F8's hub screen has no feature anywhere in the backlog. It edits display name and email, launches the avatar canvas, holds the dark-mode toggle, lists the walls, and signs out. E02-F6 covers deletion and export, neither of which is on this screen, so App Store required account deletion has no surface yet.

new_features.title: Self-only profile update endpoint
new_features.rationale: PATCH /users/{id} accepts displayName, email, avatarColor or avatarImage and authorizes from the x-user-id header rather than a client-supplied id. That authorization rule is the load-bearing part and no feature states it.

new_features.title: Change a password from settings
new_features.rationale: The password field takes keystrokes into local state and is never read by handleSave. E02-F1 covers sign-up and sign-in and says nothing about changing a credential. A field that accepts input and discards it is worse than no field.

/settings.note: Nothing in the backlog covers account and profile management. Two things on this screen need decisions, not just build. Dark mode never leaves the device (src/stores/useThemeStore.ts:113-124) while name and email round-trip, with no visual cue telling them apart, and E01-F9 rules for one theme rather than four. This screen is also the sole door to F7's member roster; that finding is recorded on /wall/[id]/members.

/share.note: E12-F4 already says it replaces this screen rather than restyling it, and it draws the boundary the two stub tiles cross. Instagram and More are inert no-ops that render as enabled buttons (app/share.tsx:503-520), and E12-F4's own words, the app's job is the file and the sheet and nothing past it, mean the fix is to delete them, not to build them. The client-side PNG capture at app/share.tsx:406-456 is the opposite of E12-F1's server-render decision, and E12-F1 already weighs and rejects device rendering, so that conflict is inside scope too.

new_features.title: Decide the fate of the on-device account switcher and the onboarding-replay toggle
new_features.rationale: Two affordances on this screen exist only for demos. The picker switches to any known account with no credentials and no network call, and a toggle forces full onboarding on every sign-in. Neither survives a real Cognito login, so someone has to say keep or cut before the rebuild copies them forward.

/sign-up.note: E02-F1 already says the POC stubbed credentials and the rebuild cannot, so the email-plus-name match is covered as work to replace. The credential-free account picker is a different thing and needs an explicit keep-or-cut call. Worth holding in mind while designing this screen: there is a sign-up, but you do it once and then stay logged in, so this screen is seen a single time per device and never again. Building it as a full peer of the daily loop overweights it.

new_features.title: Persist the onboarding step and resume there on relaunch
new_features.rationale: E02-F4 lists eight screens but says nothing about resuming a half-finished first run. Splash is only a fork because a per-user step name is persisted on every onboarding screen and clamped back to the canvas when the draft is gone, and that machinery has no feature of its own.

/splash.note: E02-F4 names the splash screen and E01-F9 owns the theme and the open question on whether it animates. What neither covers is the resume decision this screen exists to make, so one new feature carries it.

new_features.title: Guard the create-flow screens on a missing draft
new_features.rationale: The four screens after /draw all read imageRef on mount and bounce to /draw with no explanation. That is one feature, not four, and no E04 feature mentions it. It also means these routes have exactly one entry point in practice, which anyone testing or demoing by URL needs told.

/story-select.note: E04-F3 already owns the write-or-record fork and the 280 cap, and this screen is that fork. E04-F3 says to leave the record button out until Q18 is settled, and the POC ships it on every platform, so the fork as built is ahead of the feature text.

new_features.title: Wall member administration screen
new_features.rationale: E05-F1 gives members and roles on the backend. The screen that shows the roster, invites by email, removes a member, and offers leave and delete has no feature. Its gating is per action, not per screen, so any member opens it and only the creator sees the write controls.

new_features.title: Leave a wall and delete a wall, with the orphan and archive guards
new_features.rationale: E05-F1 covers joining a channel and says nothing about leaving or deleting one. Both endpoints exist in the POC with real rules, a sole-owner creator is blocked from leaving and the personal archive wall refuses delete with a 400. Those rules need a feature to live in.

new_features.title: Put a wall administration door on the wall
new_features.rationale: The only entry to this screen is /settings -> Your walls -> a wall row (app/settings.tsx:163-165). The entry point on /family was deliberately removed. F7's administration screen is reachable only through F8, so a person managing a wall has to leave the wall to do it. This is a design gap, not a build gap, and it needs a decision rather than a fix.

/wall/[id]/members.note: PR 63's finding checks out against both sources. app/settings.tsx:163-165 is the sole call site and app/family.tsx:1107-1111 records the removal of the other one. E05-F1 covers membership as data; the administration surface, the leave and delete rules, and the missing door are three separate pieces of work it does not name.

new_features.title: Prompt pack catalog and per-wall prompt injection
new_features.rationale: Nine curated packs are seeded and served, and a wall creator can write prompts from a pack onto their own wall. E03 ships one prompt a day, the same for everyone, that the app can never edit. A wall-scoped prompt set is a second prompt source with its own authorization, and the backlog has no feature for it.

new_features.title: Author a custom prompt for one wall
new_features.rationale: A creator types a prompt of up to MAX_CUSTOM_PROMPT_LENGTH characters and it becomes a live prompt on that wall. E03-F4 routes drafted prompts through Scribl editors before anyone sees them. This path has no editorial review at all, which is a policy question as much as a build one.

/wall/[id]/prompt-packs.note: Prompt packs are not in the backlog. E03 is explicit that prompts stay curated by Scribl's program team and that the app never edits them. Packs used to be named only inside E18-F2's parked challenges concept, and E18-F2 was retired on 2026-09-01 precisely because this screen is what challenges became, so the capability is now shipped in the POC and filed nowhere at all. This screen lets a wall creator add prompts with no editorial step, which contradicts E03's stated premise rather than extending it, so it gets net-new features and a decision.

new_features.title: Pick prompts from a pack and add them to a wall
new_features.rationale: Step two of the picker is the only screen in the pair that writes. A creator selects up to five prompts and they persist to the wall. The cap of five stands in for a spoken instruction of a couple and should be ratified once here rather than rediscovered from a code comment.

/wall/[id]/prompt-packs/[packId].note: Same gap as step one, and this is the half that changes state. Selecting a sixth prompt is a silent client-side no-op with no message (:39), so the cap needs a UX rule as well as a number.

new_features.title: Edit a caption after it is submitted
new_features.rationale: The footer copy under the button promises the caption stays editable after publish. No caption edit surface exists anywhere in the app, and E05-F4's response detail is read plus reactions only. Either build the editor or change the copy.

/write.note: E04-F3 covers this screen's substance and the 280 cap is the same shared constant, not a lookalike number. The one thing the feature does not account for is the promise this screen makes about editing captions later.
